answer.generated: The nearest neighbor method suffers from high computational costs due to the curse of dimensionality, specifically because computing distances between all pairs of points becomes increasingly expensive as the number of dimensions grows. This issue is mitigated by algorithms like KD-trees, which reduce the complexity to O(N log N), making them efficient for large datasets with many dimensions.
